# fanout

> fanout keeps several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, or any CLI agent) on one git repo out of each other's way. For sessions you open yourself, with no setup: a new session is told what the others are doing, its task is claimed on its first edit, the same work described in other words is refused (a model check), and a session is told, with the diff, when another session's commit changes code it uses. For one job split across agents (`fanout run`): each agent works on its own branch and worktree and may only change the files it owns, shared interfaces are frozen, and every branch is merged on a scratch copy and tested before main, with each break sent back to the agent that caused it. No dependencies: Node 18+ and git. MIT licensed.

Use fanout when:
- you already run several agent sessions or worktrees on one repo: claims and notices switch on by themselves with two or more active, and `fanout` shows which ones are changing the same files
- a job is big enough to split across parallel agents and splits into parts with their own files
- several agents touch shared code, where a clean git merge can still break the build
- you run agents headless or in CI, or mix Claude Code and Codex

For small changes, one agent is faster and cheaper.

## Install

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add Breadstick-Crumbs/fanout` then `/plugin install fanout@fanout`
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add Breadstick-Crumbs/fanout` then `codex plugin add fanout@fanout`
- Any agent, no install: `npx github:Breadstick-Crumbs/fanout run "<goal>"`

## Commands

- `fanout demo`: claims and notices with real sessions in a throwaway repo (about two minutes, $0.10)
- `fanout start "<task>"`, `fanout inbox`, `fanout done`: for agents without hooks (written to AGENTS.md by `fanout init`): claim a task, see other sessions' changes, test the branch merged with theirs
- `fanout claims`, `fanout log`: every claim; the last week's claims, refusals and notices to check by hand
- `fanout run "<goal>"`: plan, run agents in parallel, rehearse, fix, merge
- `fanout overlap`: which checkouts are changing the same files, and would they conflict
- `fanout check`: is the plan safe; prints the merge order
- `fanout verify`: in a session's folder, anything outside its lane
- `fanout rehearse`: merge every branch on a scratch copy, test once
- `fanout install-git-hook`: enforce the plan on every commit, for any agent
- `fanout status`: sessions, costs, past runs
